children: A bipartisan AI safety bill from senators Amy Klobuchar, Ted Cruz, and John Thune may be introduced as early as next week,

Klobuchar told Semafor in a statement that she is working on a bipartisan agreement on “legislation for commonsense guardrails to address the risks posed by AI systems…it’s clear we need to act now and not wait.”

The legislation is being viewed by some lawmakers as the most viable path for passing AI safeguards before 2027. AI companies and public advocacy groups are already providing feedback on the draft, which has not yet been publicly released.
The effort gained urgency after a departing Anthropic researcher warned that people developing AI “earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” according to Semafor.

“AI is advancing at an extraordinary pace, and some of the risks are dangerous and frightening…I’m working with Senators Amy Klobuchar and John Thune on legislation to address catastrophic risks involving biological or nuclear threats,” Cruz posted on X.

Meanwhile, Sen. Bernie Sanders is reportedly preparing to introduce a bill that would ban superintelligence and pause AI development. He also plans to convene experts for a bipartisan briefing next week following recent AI security incidents.

Rep. Ro Khanna has proposed a five-step plan to “urgently address the potential harms of AI,” including certification requirements for new models, liability and criminal penalties for AI companies, and the creation of a new federal agency.

OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane wrote in a Wednesday blog post that the company wants to work with Congress on national AI safety regulation due to “a new chapter in AI capabilities,” citing its own models and research.

“We need to meet this moment with a bias toward meaningful action over policy perfection,” Lehane wrote, adding that several “serious” AI frontier safety proposals are circulating in Congress and it needs to act before it adjourns. “The AI policy window is open, for now. We intend to use it.”

title: Bipartisan AI safety bill may be introduced as early as next week as AI fears mount
